apps/desktop/electron/services/fault-inj.content: This assertion (and every other `staleFrames` assertion in the suite: tests 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and `m.staleFrames`) can never fail. `runFaultSuite` hardcodes `staleFrames: 0` in the returned result (line 151) and in each measurement (line 146) — the value is never derived from actual deliveries. So the suite's headline promise ("goes red if ... stale frames ... regress") is not actually verified by these tests. Either make the engine compute `staleFrames` from real delivery/tick state so this assertion is meaningful, or assert on something the port can actually observe (e.g. that every delivered frame index is strictly increasing per device).

The `workerkill` scenario is registered but its measurement is never asserted — only `hostkill` is checked. A regression in worker-kill recovery (wrong `recoveryFrames`, no `othersContinued`, frames continuing to the killed device) would leave this test green. Also, the reload assertion only counts deliveries at frame 30; it does not verify the payload, so a broken reload that emits `"held"`/all-off while still delivering two frames would pass. Add assertions on the workerkill measurement and on the reload payload.

This aggregate count over the combined duplication+reorder window is a masking assertion: 20 deliveries over frames [30,50) can still be 20 if, e.g., duplication caused extra deliveries on some frames while reorder dropped the same number on others. It proves nothing about per-frame duplicate resolution. Assert per-delivery identity instead, e.g. that each (device, frame) in the window appears exactly once.

`toHaveLength(120)` is effectively tautological here: port-conflict and multicast-blocked are discovery-plane faults that never touch the delivery path in `runFaultSuite`, so this count is always frames × devices regardless of whether frames actually "kept flowing" correctly. The `discoveryDegradedFrames` check below is the only meaningful assertion. Consider asserting per-device frame continuity (every device delivered on every frame in the window) so a broken failover that stalls delivery would be caught.

apps/desktop/electron/updater/index.test.content: The requirement being tested is "no modal", but this assertion is ineffective. `state.notice` is just a status string; asserting it does not literally contain the word `"dialog"` cannot detect whether a modal/dialog was actually opened elsewhere in the flow. Assert the actual no-modal contract instead (e.g., that no modal-opening API is called, or that the returned state carries no modal/result flag), or drop the misleading assertion.

The precedence between `skip-disabled` and `defer-live` is never constrained: every `decideUpdateCheck` call here passes `checkOnLaunch: true`. Since the implementation returns `defer-live` before checking `checkOnLaunch` (index.ts lines 18-27), a regression that swapped the ordering — e.g. returning `skip-disabled` while Live is active when checks are disabled — would go undetected. Add cases with `checkOnLaunch: false` combined with `liveActive: true` and `showLoaded: true` and assert the intended action.

Since `electron-builder.cjs` explicitly targets Windows (`win` → NSIS, x64+arm64), running `yarn build` on a Windows dev machine/CI agent will fail at the last step. apps/desktop/package.json.content: `electron-builder` is invoked by these scripts but is not declared in this package's `devDependencies` (only in the root `package.json`). Resolution currently relies on hoisting via `nodeLinker: node-modules`; if the linker is switched to PnP or the root dep is removed, packaging breaks. Declare the tool in this package's `devDependencies` (e.g. `"electron-builder": "^26"`) so the dependency is explicit and version-consistent.

`dist:package:dir` omits `node scripts/fetch-vendor.mjs`, but `electron-builder.cjs` unconditionally lists `vendor` under `extraResources`. On a clean checkout (no `apps/desktop/vendor/`) electron-builder will fail because the `extraResources.from: "vendor"` directory does not exist, so this script produces a broken/incomplete package. Run `fetch-vendor` here as well (matching `dist:package`).

All internal workspace packages are referenced with a semver range (`^0.1.0`) instead of the `workspace:` protocol. Because `^0.1.0` allows `<0.2.0`, any workspace package bumped to `0.2.0` would silently stop matching the local workspace and be resolved from the registry, causing version/schema drift between packages in the same monorepo. Prefer `workspace:^0.1.0` (this repo uses Yarn 4) to guarantee local linking and an explicit version contract.

apps/desktop/src/app/resolve-live.test.t.content: This assertion only holds because `buildLive`'s one-shot fallback uses `a.state.playheadSeconds` **directly as a beat** (`beatA = beat?.a ?? a.state.playheadSeconds`), while the cursor path uses `beat?.a` which is a real beat number. The two paths therefore mix units (seconds vs beats). `playheadSeconds: 10` with `effectiveBpm: 128` should be ~21.3 beats if it were derived from the grid, yet the test hard-codes 10 — so it locks in the seconds-as-beats conflation and would not catch a fallback bug; it also cannot distinguish a correct snapshot beat from this coincidence. Add a case where the snapshot would yield a different beat than `playheadSeconds` (or derive the expected value from the grid) so the fallback semantics are actually exercised.

The file header claims "the live cursor's computed beat must reach the render sink" (AL-FLOW-003), but both tests only inspect `buildLive`'s return value. The regression being guarded against actually lives in `useLiveCursor` (beatRef.current → `buildLive(..., beatRef.current)` → `set({ live, liveBeat: live.beat })`). A regression where the cursor stops forwarding its computed beat into `buildLive`, or where the returned beat is never written to the store, would still pass here. Add a test that drives `useLiveCursor`/the beat-forwarding integration, or assert on the store sink, to make the stated guarantee meaningful.

The cursor override is passed as an opaque `{ a: 70, b: 1 }` literal (which field is the beat is not documented), and only deck A is asserted — `b` and multi-deck wiring are never verified. Also untested: the `buildLive(...) === null` path (empty decks), the beat exactly on a section boundary (`startBeat`/`endBeat`), and a beat past the last section. These are cheap cases that would catch off-by-one / range regressions in the section lookup and the fallback defaulting. Consider extracting a named helper for the cursor argument and covering the boundary + deck B cases.

apps/desktop/src/app/security.test.ts.content: `registerAudioWindow` mutates the module-level `audioWindowUrls` Set and there is no `afterEach`/cleanup (and no `unregisterAudioWindow` export to reset it). The `isAudioWindow(...)` assertion below therefore depends on execution order: if any earlier test (in this file or a re-ordered suite) registers the same origin, the `expect(...).toBe(false)` check is no longer meaningful, and the registration leaks into subsequent tests. Wrap the mutation in a reset/unregister helper (or `vi.resetModules()` + re-import) so each test starts from a known empty state.

The CSP parsing here is evadable: `.find(d => d.startsWith("script-src"))` only inspects the FIRST directive whose name begins with `script-src`, so an additional `script-src-elem`/second `script-src` slips past the exact-equality check. More importantly, the loop below explicitly `continue`s on `connect-src`, and the only global remote check is `not.toContain("https:")`, so a permissive `connect-src 'self' http://evil.example` (remote HTTP target) passes this suite unnoticed. Assert per-directive that no non-local origin appears (excluding the exact known-local entries) and iterate every `script-src*` directive instead of only the first.

apps/desktop/src/app/security.test.ts.content: These assertions inspect only the object returned by `securitySettings()`, which is data, not enforcement. In `main.ts`, `allowNewWindow` and `permissions.audioCaptureOrigins/midiOrigins` are never read at runtime — the new-window handler hardcodes `{ action: "deny" }` and the permission handler decides via `isAudioWindow(url)`. So this test can stay green even if the actual window hardening is removed (e.g. deleting `setWindowOpenHandler`, or changing the permission filter) — exactly the regression T-SEC-03 claims to catch. Either wire these fields into `main.ts` consumers, or assert observable behavior (handlers/`webPreferences`) instead of the config shape.
